title: Correcting a reading recomputes the rate at once
custom_preconds:
1. Sign in to the Maintenance Reminders QA build as an Owner/Admin (any user who can open Settings > Maintenance and create and edit work orders and customers).
  2. Open Settings > Maintenance, press New schedule and create a throwaway schedule 'ZZAUTOTEST Reading seed' holding one routine service per reading you will seed, named 'ZZ Seed 1', 'ZZ Seed 2' and so on, each with a Calendar trigger of Every 12 months and no canned lines. Save. (If it already exists, reuse it.)
  3. Open Customers > 'ZZAUTOTEST Fleet Co' > Assets and create unit 'ZZAUTOTEST 506' with New Asset, leaving Mileage and Engine Hours empty. On its Maintenance tab press Enroll in Schedule, choose 'ZZAUTOTEST Reading seed' and give every seed service a last service date five years ago (for example 6 Oct 2021), so each seed service reads Overdue and shows on the work order card; press Enroll.
  4. Readings for 'ZZAUTOTEST 506' (oldest first): 1) 28 Jun 2026 · 333,000 mileage; 2) 28 Jul 2026 · 335,100 mileage; 3) 27 Aug 2026 · 338,100 mileage; 4) 26 Sep 2026 · 341,100 mileage. Dates are for a run on 6 Oct 2026. On another day, move every date by the same number of days and seed and read on the same day, because an estimate and a reading's age both count days up to today.
  5. Seed each reading in the table, oldest first: open Work Orders and press New Work Order for the unit; type the reading's mileage in the work order's Mileage field (and its engine hours in Engine Hours where the table gives one; leave the field untouched where it does not) and save; expand the Maintenance schedule card, open the three-dot menu of a seed service not used yet, choose Mark complete, keep On a work order with this work order chosen, set Reset date to the reading's date and press Mark complete. That work order's values become readings dated the Reset date. Confirm any warning the field shows.
  6. Do not remove the seed schedule yet. Note the work order that carries the last reading (341,100).
custom_steps:
1. Open unit 506's Maintenance tab and read the Mileage card's rate and current estimate.
  2. Work out by hand: (341,100 − 333,000) ÷ 90 days = 90 a day = 630 a week; estimate 341,100 + 90 × 10 = 342,000.
  3. Open the work order that carries the last reading and correct its Mileage field to 342,000; save.
  4. Reopen the Maintenance tab and read the rate and current estimate again.
  5. Work out by hand: (342,000 − 333,000) ÷ 90 = 100 a day = 700 a week; estimate 342,000 + 100 × 10 = 343,000.
  6. Remove the unit from 'ZZAUTOTEST Reading seed' (Remove from schedule).
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Before the correction the card reads 630 a week and a current estimate of 342,000.
  • Straight after the correction, without waiting overnight, it reads 700 a week and 343,000: the rate is worked out again from the stored pairs.
  • How to correct an older reading by hand is not stated by the spec (open question); this case corrects the latest one.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-3780 (Maintenance Reminders); story SV-10568 (S11, Rate, estimate and confidence); story SV-10567 (S10, Enter a reading); Chunk 2 MR (Confluence 897679389) as edited 5 October 2026, S11, S10; Plan 1 — Track, act, clear — Technical Implementation Plan, section 3.2, TD-06; read 6 Oct 2026. Source-verified 6 October 2026; not yet build-verified.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S11-R7: “The rate will never be cached incrementally. A correction anywhere in the history recomputes it”
  • S10-E3: “A correction recomputes the rate from stored pairs and moves every threshold and queued reminder”
  • Plan 1 §3.2 TD-06: “one row per (WO, meter), updated in place on each WO edit that changes the value (TD-34)”
  • S18-R19: “Mark complete On a work order also records that work order's mileage and engine hours as the asset's readings, dated the Reset date”
